- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00), model often overreacts to recent highs; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 7–14 day horizon.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–7 days.  
- If 3+ consecutive days of downward trend in history, model underestimates; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast.  
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); adjust downward by 1–2% for first 5 days if sentiment is flat or negative.  
- Mean reversion bias: if price deviates >3σ from 30-day moving average, forecast should revert toward MA within 10–15 days.  
- If sentiment history shows no change for 5+ days, model tends to drift; apply 0.5–1% downward correction for 7–10 day horizon.
